$comment: THE SYNTHESIS ROUTER's configuration. This is `sutra route` — the pipeline's
own model chain. It is NOT your harness's chat model, and Sutra never reads,
writes or owns that (S9.4: touch only your own keys, ever).
D8: the upstream system had two routers with different provider orders, and
editing one fixed nothing in the other. `sutra doctor` shows both side by
side, and every generated page records which one served it.
SHIPS ACCOUNT-NEUTRAL. No model id tied to anyone's account, no `key_env`
name implying a particular subscription, no free-tier assumption. The leak
D5: adding a provider here WITHOUT adding its key shape to
secret-patterns.json is a bug — a configurable provider the scanner cannot
see. CI asserts the two stay in step.
EVERYTHING HERE IS OPTIONAL. Sutra's default is deterministic-only: with no
provider configured at all, retrieval, tiering, linking, the graph and cited
answers still work. A model adds prose synthesis on top of them and nothing
else. `enabled: false` on every entry below is the shipped default and is a
$providers_comment: ORDER IS THE FALLBACK ORDER. `local: true` means the model runs on THIS
machine, which is what makes it eligible for private and secret content.
`local_only` content is served by a local provider or by nothing. There is
no configuration in this file that routes it to a hosted one, and
Select-Provider filters by tier before it considers anything else.

providers.notes: An on-machine model. The ONLY kind eligible for private or secret content. Set `model` to whatever you have pulled; Sutra ships no default because a model id you do not have produces a confusing 404 rather than a clear 'not configured'.
Hosted. NOTE: free tiers have low daily caps. A maintenance job must never consume the quota a quality job depends on — see `tasks` below.
Fast, not reasoning-capable, so it is excluded from synthesis by policy rather than by hoping the router picks something better.

D19 lived here: `base_url_env` is normally unset, and reading it unsafely threw before any network I/O — 2,109 times, every one recorded as a provider failure. `Get-EnvSafe` and the `parse_error` status exist because of this entry.

$tasks_comment: PER-TASK POLICY. `requires_reasoning` is a FLOOR, not a preference: a
provider that fails it is excluded and NOTHING re-admits it (D17 — the
upstream fallback re-admitted the provider the floor had just excluded, and
a reasoning task was served by a model structurally barred from reasoning).
`quota_class` exists because a COST BUG CAUSED A QUALITY BUG upstream:
curate and organize burned ~2,570 calls a night on unchanged content and
exhausted the quota synthesis depended on. Maintenance work must never
consume the budget quality work needs.

synthesize_draft.notes: Writes a durable page from an extract. NO INPUT CLIP, EVER (D1) — if a source exceeds the window, chunk-and-merge or refuse. A 6,000-char prefix produces a confident, fluent, 400-word page that is wrong in specifics, and nothing in the corpus looks anomalous.

answer.notes: Prose synthesis over retrieved sources. With no provider, `sutra ask` returns the cited context block — which is a real answer, not a failure.

$degradation_comment: Degradation is allowed. Silent degradation is not.
Every stage may produce less than its ideal output. What it may never do is
produce less and report success. An unconfigured provider is a WARNING
naming the exact environment variable; an empty chain THROWS; a page that
no model wrote simply has no `synthesis_provider:` in its frontmatter, and
that absence is itself the signal.
